desc:
A company is flying 2n candidates in for interviews. The entry costs[i] = [a, b] is the price to send candidate i to city A (a) or to city B (b).

Exactly n candidates must go to each city. Return the minimum total cost.

costs = [[10,20],[30,200],[400,50],[30,20]] -> 110

Send the first two to city A (10 + 30) and the last two to city B (50 + 20).
hints: Imagine first sending everyone to city A. Then you must move exactly half of the candidates to B.
Moving candidate i from A to B changes the total by b - a. You want the n most negative (or smallest) changes.
Sort the candidates by a - b. The first n (those who prefer A most strongly) go to A; the remaining n go to B.
editorial: Let diff = a - b. Sending a candidate to A instead of B costs diff more (negative means A is cheaper). The total cost equals sum(b) + sum of diff over the group sent to A. Since the group sent to A has exactly n candidates, we minimise by choosing the n candidates with the smallest a - b.

So sort by a - b, send the first n to A and the last n to B, and add up. If two candidates have the same difference, either assignment gives the same total. Sorting costs O(n log n), and the answer is at most 10,000 × 10,000 = 108.
